URL: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iranian-flights-cancelled-new-us-d-day-sanctions-take-effect-saudis-say-they-2026-09-24/
Reuters — published 24 Sep 2026 15:37 BST, updated 18:27 BST (Dubai/Riyadh)

HEADLINE: New US sanctions shut down Iranian flights

Iranian airlines were barred from neighbouring countries including the UAE and Oman on Thursday in response to new US sanctions — the first big impact of a shift in US policy to target companies in third countries that do business with Iran.

- The General Civil Aviation Authority of the United Arab Emirates, the Middle East's biggest travel hub, said that as a result of the new US policy it was suspending all flights by Iranian airlines until further notice.
- Iran's Tasnim news agency reported flights had also been shut down to Oman, Georgia and Azerbaijan, and to Baghdad. Authorities were working to route flights to another Iraqi airport, in Najaf.
- Washington had announced it would sanction any global company doing business with Iranian airlines after September 23, aiming to ground Iran's entire civil fleet worldwide.
- Tehran's Imam Khomeini Airport listed scheduled arrivals and departures on Thursday to and from Afghanistan, Armenia, China, Iraq, Pakistan, Tajikistan and Turkey — but no flights to or from the nearby Gulf states.
- On Wednesday a senior Iranian official threatened to make airports "unusable" in any regional country that abides by the US ban.
- Trump referred to the new secondary-sanctions strategy last month as "economic D-Day", comparing it to the WWII assault on Nazi-controlled France.

QUOTE (retired teacher in Tehran, to Reuters by text message, name withheld): "We are living in an open-air prison."

SAUDI ARABIA / HOUTHIS:
- Saudi Arabia said it intercepted six Houthi ballistic missiles on Thursday, after issuing emergency alerts for areas including the holy city of Mecca, Jeddah and Yanbu, the main Saudi Red Sea oil port.
- QUOTE (statement from the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis in Yemen): "Any escalation and violations by the terrorist Houthi militia will be dealt with firmly."
- Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group attacked Saudi military sites in Jazan province bordering Yemen — operations rooms, command and control centres, weapons depots, missile launch sites and military camps.
- Sources in the Saudi-backed Yemeni government said forces repelled overnight Houthi attacks on a key supply route to Aden. The Houthis seized Yemen's entire Red Sea coast this month and are pushing into highlands near Taiz, keeping pressure on the Hejat al-Abd mountain pass.
- More than 700 people have been killed and thousands wounded in the latest fighting, according to the United Nations. Nearly 130,000 Yemenis have been displaced within the country; more than 3,000 have fled by boat across the Red Sea to Africa.

CONTEXT: The war, which Trump launched alongside Israel in February as "Operation Epic Fury", has disrupted global energy supplies, killed thousands and pushed up oil prices. Iran already faces a US naval blockade of its ports.
